stories.title: In hard-hitting speech, Bilawal says system was ‘made to collapse’
summary: Amid debate on a “system reset” in the country, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Tuesday that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

In his address, Bilawal said that it was the opposition’s role in the Parliament to criticise the government. “It is the opposition’s right to criticise you, and however he (Fazl) does it, it is their right,” Bilawal said.

Bilawal remarked that the opposition had the “most patriotic” role in the Parliament. “For any government to question the patriotism of an opposition member [..] it is not only an injustice to that parliament or to the system, but the biggest injustice to the country,” he added.

stories.title: CDF Munir discusses avenues for enhancing bilateral defence cooperation with UK army, Turkish air chiefs
summary: According to the statement, the visit reflected the shared resolve of Pakistan and the UK to deepen defence cooperation and strengthen bilateral military ties.

Separately, Commander of the Turkish Air Force General Rafet Dalkıran also called on the CDF at GHQ, where matters of mutual interest, regional security dynamics and avenues to enhance bilateral defence cooperation were discussed, the military said.

The visiting dignitary reciprocated the strengthening of bilateral defence ties, appreciated the professionalism of the Pakistan Armed Forces and acknowledged the country’s contributions to regional peace and stability, the ISPR added.

stories.title: Pakistan, Sri Lanka docked WTC points for slow over-rates in first Test
summary: Pakistan and Sri Lanka have been penalised for maintaining slow over-rates in the drawn first Test of their two-match ICC World Test Championship (WTC) series, with Pakistan losing five points and Sri Lanka suffering a 15-point deduction.

Match referee Dean Cosker of the ICC International Panel imposed the sanctions after Pakistan were found five overs short of the required rate and Sri Lanka 15 overs behind, after time allowances were taken into account.
Consequently, Pakistan were fined 25 per cent of their match fees, while Sri Lanka received the maximum 50 per cent fine.

stories.title: Autopsy reveals multiple injuries on teenage domestic worker found dead at FIA official’s residence in Islamabad
summary: ISLAMABAD: The autopsy report of a 13-year-old domestic worker, who was found dead at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) official on Sunday night, suggests that she had been subjected to repeated physical assaults.

Old burn scars on the back, a thickened scar on the right upper thigh, darkened and swollen skin around both knees and the left thigh, swelling in the knee joint and a non-healing wound on the outer side of the left knee were also found.
An Islamabad police officer said Fatima had been working as a domestic help at the official’s residence for a couple of years, dating back to when he was serving in the capital police.

stories.title: Fire engulfs glass factory in Karachi's Baldia Town: rescue official
summary: KARACHI: A massive fire broke out at an industrial unit in Karachi’s Baldia Town on Tuesday morning, reportedly during the refilling of an underground oil tank by a tanker, rescue officials said.

Screen grab from a video of a fire in Karachi’s Baldia Town, on November 17, 2026. — Rescue 1122 “During the preliminary probe, it emerged that an oil tanker was refilling an underground oil tank when it caught fire and exploded,” the spokesperson said.
In a statement, Site-B police said the fire broke out at the Al-Hamad Plastic Factory in the Rasheedabad area of Baldia Town.

stories.title: Inside Deutsche Bank: Leak of 15 million files exposes secrets, scandals and double standards of global financial giant
summary: In 2015, despite mounting adverse media reports and its own suspicious activity reports, or SARs, surrounding Jho Low, Deutsche Bank continued to process millions in transfers linked to the Malaysian financier.

In the investigation proceedings of the public prosecutor’s office in Frankfurt in connection with two suspicious activity reports (SAR) filed by Deutsche Bank in the correspondent banking business, the bank accepted a fine of €7.01 million.
Deutsche Bank continued doing business with him.

stories.title: FCC directs LDA to stop ‘frivolous litigation’ against family of martyred national hero Rashid Minhas
summary: During subsequent execution proceedings, the LDA objected, arguing that the 14-marla plot in Gulberg-III, Lahore, was evacuee property acquired by the authority for the development of the Gulberg-III scheme.
The LHC had consequently directed the LDA to stop claiming ownership of the disputed land, which had already become part of the Gulberg-III scheme, the FCC observed.

The high court’s judgment was subsequently challenged by the LDA before the Supreme Court, which dismissed the petition, holding that the authority had no ownership rights over the land, as it had already been transferred by the Settlement Department to the occupants.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkmenistan to convene steering committee for TAPI gas pipeline, stress engagement among partner countries
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday discussed the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline with a delegation led by Turkmenistan’s Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov.
The discussion took place at the 6th Session of the Pakistan–Turkmenistan Joint Intergovernmental Commission (JIC), which was held in Islamabad on Tuesday.
In June 2023, Pakistan and Turkmenistan signed a joint implementation plan to execute the TAPI gas pipeline project.

stories.title: Pakistan’s pace trio routs Sri Lanka for 98 before openers take control in second Test
summary: Pakistan’s fast bowlers produced a devastating display to dismiss Sri Lanka for a paltry 98 on the opening day of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday, before openers Tayyab Arif and Azan Awais made a confident start to the reply.
Sri Lanka, who were asked to bat after Pakistan won the toss, struggled against the pace and movement on offer, losing wickets at regular intervals before being bowled out in 35.3 overs.
Pakistan’s response began cautiously as Sri Lanka’s new-ball bowlers found movement.

stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers, police clash in fresh wage protest
summary: Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed.
A wage board meeting scheduled for Monday was postponed after a member representing the garment workers said he was unwell, a source in BGMEA told AFP.
The country’s garment industry makes clothes for some of the world’s best-known brands but the sector has been marred by longstanding disputes over wages, working conditions and labour rights.

stories.title: CDF Munir underscores importance of sustained engagement, mutual trust in meeting with Iran’s Araghchi
summary: Pakistan has been mediating between Washington and Tehran, making efforts for an end to a war that began with US attacks on Iran on February 28.
Pakistan’s mediation Pakistan’s efforts for peace between the two sides began soon after the war.
But Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday that Islamabad had not given up on its diplomatic efforts for a peaceful resolution to the US-Iran war.

stories.title: Punjab’s Mustafa Sheharyar Rana wins three silver medals at National Swimming Championship
summary: en-year-old swimmer Mustafa Sheharyar Rana delivered an impressive performance at the National Age Group Swimming Championship, winning three silver medals in three events while representing Punjab.

Competing in the Under-10 category, Mustafa secured an individual silver medal in the 50m Backstroke and contributed to two silver medal-winning relay teams: 4×100m Freestyle Relay: Silver alongside Abdul Rafay, Omer Hassan and Zain Razaque.
His performance also builds on his earlier success at the CM Punjab Age Group Inter-School Swimming Championship, where he was recognized as the fastest Under-10 swimmer.

stories.title: Vinicius hat-trick inspires Brazil rout
summary: Vinicius Jr continued his return to form with a hat-trick in Brazil's 7-0 friendly rout of Singapore on Tuesday as the ‌five-times world champions bounced back from their dramatic 3-2 defeat by Japan.
The forward, who scored both Brazil's goals against Japan, completed his hat-trick inside 21 minutes.
His Real Madrid teammate Endrick, along ⁠with Estevao Willian and Rayan, also netted and Singapore right back Raoul Suhaimi added to the hosts' misery with an own goal.

summary: Vance’s comments come as the US and Iran remain locked in a conflict while debate intensifies over it costs and duration. “We are not going to allow this to become a 10- or 15-year commitment, or frankly, even a two-year commitment,” Vance said.
Asked whether there were differences between him and Trump over the war, he rejected the suggestion, saying there was no disagreement among senior administration officials.

He acknowledged, however, that the conflict had carried political costs, particularly through higher gasoline and energy prices. “Politically, yes, and I think the president himself has absolutely said this as well.

stories.title: West Bank’s displaced Palestinians hold little hope for post-Netanyahu era
summary: After Israeli forces pushed him and thousands of others out of the West Bank refugee camp of Tulkarem last year, Adel Darsieh held onto his hope of returning home, but it is fading fast.

Displaced Palestinians from Tulkarem refugee camp wait outside a charitable association to receive food, near the city of Tulkarem in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on November 11, 2026. —AFP For Palestinian families, it is a second form of displacement.

He pointed to how Israel, soon after the election, ended an operation in Hebron that displaced 3,000 Palestinians, which was launched after gunmen shot dead two Israeli soldiers. ‘Scale of suffering’ Even if residents could return, much of the camp has been destroyed.

stories.title: French cricket 'dying' as federation crisis and chaos deepens
summary: AFP spoke to the president of the France Gymkhana club, Rizwan Babri, the president of another club and the team manager from a third club who all confirmed they wanted Balane to resign and for France Cricket to be restructured.

It began when France 24 broke an explosive story in 2023 about clubs in the country faking women’s matches, apparently so France Cricket could benefit from hundreds of thousands of dollars of ICC funding.
France Cricket have always denied that women’s ghost matches took place — Balane told the BBC in June that it had “never” happened.

stories.title: Afghanistan’s ‘war on women’: How an exiled newsroom finds ways to support journalists under Taliban rule
summary: In Afghanistan, women journalists work covertly and communicate using encrypted platforms with colleagues abroad, finding creative ways to continue reporting under the Taliban’s repressive regime.
Yet, despite significant restrictions – Zahra emphasises the unrelenting determination of many Afghan women journalists to keep reporting.

The pseudonyms and bylines used by Zan Times reporters, Zahra said, are also meant to help the journalists eventually gain public recognition for their work when it is safe to do so. “In my lifetime, five regimes have changed in Afghanistan, and I’m not even that old.

stories.title: Dhoni takes up Chennai’s mentor role
summary: Former India cricket captain MS Dhoni has retired as a player in the Indian Premier League and will take up a mentoring role with Chennai Super Kings, the franchise said on Tuesday.
The 45-year-old wicketkeeper-batter, who last played for India in 2019, led Chennai to five IPL titles, establishing the franchise as one of the tournament's most successful teams.
Dhoni scored 5,314 runs for Chennai, making him the franchise's second-highest run-scorer.

stories.title: Former Wall Street regulator warns AI bubble could burst, trigger recession
summary: Former Wall Street regulator Gary Gensler on Tuesday warned that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence has created an economic bubble that could collapse and trigger a recession before the 2028 US presidential election, according to CNN.

Read: In China, the AI bubble has already burst Gensler argued that history shows how periods of rapid technological innovation and massive investment eventually reach a turning point, when growth slows, and markets begin to contract.

He cited the railway boom, the widespread adoption of electricity in the 1920s and the internet boom of the 1990s as examples of major innovations that attracted substantial investment before experiencing significant economic setbacks.

stories.title: US naval presence in Middle East exceeds peak of Iran war: Israeli institute
summary: The current US naval presence in the Middle East region exceeds the level recorded during the peak of the US-Israeli war on Iran in February and March, an Israeli security institute said on Tuesday.
It did not provide a figure for the current number of US forces or naval vessels deployed in the region.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, while Tehran responded with attacks on Israel and what it says are US military facilities in Arab countries.

stories.title: 2 trains collide near Prague, leaving dozens injured, disrupting rail services
summary: Two trains collided near Prague’s main railway station on Tuesday morning, leaving dozens of passengers injured, several of them seriously, the Czech News Agency reported.
Prague emergency services spokesman Karel Kirs said several passengers had suffered serious injuries, with some facing life-threatening complications.
All seriously injured passengers were taken to hospitals in Prague, while everyone aboard the two trains was evacuated, Kirs said.

stories.title: Bilawal calls for 'political reset', says system 'deliberately destroyed'
summary: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Tuesday called for a "political reset" to restore confidence in the country's institutions, saying the political system had not collapsed on its own but had been deliberately dismantled.
He said the country could not function without recognising the opposition party as a legitimate political stakeholder.
"PTI is a political stakeholder and a political reality in this country.

stories.title: Aiman Khan, Muneeb Butt honoured at British Parliament
summary: Actors Aiman Khan and Muneeb Butt received special recognition at the British Parliament in London for their contributions to drama, entertainment and the promotion of Pakistani culture internationally.

Both Aiman and Butt also shared videos from the event, including clips of their speeches, expressing gratitude for the honour and the affection they received from the Pakistani community in the United Kingdom.
View this post on Instagram Addressing the gathering, Aiman thanked those who attended the event and said she felt blessed to have received the recognition.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns Israeli attacks in Syria, calls for withdrawal from occupied territories
summary: Speaking at a briefing on the political and humanitarian situation in Syria, Ambassador Shah said Israeli violations undermined Syria’s security and obstructed its recovery.
Pakistan welcomed the Syrian government’s efforts to advance the political transition, rebuild national institutions and strengthen engagement with regional and international partners.
Ambassador Shah called for sustained humanitarian assistance, saying the scale of Syria’s needs required predictable support and effective cooperation with the Syrian government.

stories.title: Pirwadhai bus stand revenue rises to Rs140m
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Regional Transport Authority (RTA) Rawalpindi has increased the annual income of Pirwadhai General Bus Stand from Rs25 million to Rs140 million by bringing 500 additional buses to operate from the facility.
Earlier, mismanagement of the bus stand affairs had forced transporters to operate buses from illegal bus stands,” he said.
He said around 850 buses currently operated from Pirwadhai General Bus Stand to different parts of the country.

stories.title: Handcuffed suspect injured in ‘encounter’ in Islamabad
summary: The suspect offered his assistance in the recovery of motorcycles and their parts, the FIR said, adding that a police team raided the hideout and recovered the motorcycles.
In the meantime four persons armed with weapons appeared and started firing at the police team from different directions and set free the under custody suspect.
Later the police team chased the attacker and found the suspect injured.

stories.title: Joint investigation team to probe illegal gold mining in KP: Samar
summary: Ms Samar said videos of illegal mining had brought the matter into the public domain and that allegations had emerged about the involvement of political figures, their relatives and alleged frontmen, as well as some officials of the local administration, police and bureaucracy.
The adviser said that action against illegal mining was not politically motivated and said the investigation would establish the facts and determine responsibility.
She expressed concern over allegations that money generated through illegal mining could reach elements involved in attacks on security forces and civilians.

stories.title: Two held in Islamabad for Rs5m UK work visa fraud
summary: According to the FIA, the suspects, in alleged connivance with a third accomplice, Tariq Bashir, lured the citizen with the promise of arranging a UK work visa for his wife and received a total of Rs5,042,000 and 200 British pounds.
Initial investigation revealed that the suspects allegedly also prepared a fake experience certificate for visa processing.
Despite rejection of the visa application by the UK Home Office, the suspects neither provided the visa nor returned the money.

stories.title: Man found murdered in Rawalpindi farmhouse
summary: RAWALPINDI: A man was found murdered in a farmhouse in the limits of Chakri police station on Sunday, police said.
After breaking the lock, they found the caretaker’s residential quarters also locked.
The complainant suspected that Faqir Taj had murdered the unidentified person, locked the body inside the room and fled with his wife and children.

stories.title: ADB approves $500m loan to support Pakistan's pension reforms
summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Tuesday approved a $500 million results-based loan to help Pakistan reform its federal civil pension system.

According to a statement issued by the ADB, the reforms would help contain rising pension-related fiscal pressures, strengthen pension system sustainability, and expand fiscal space for development and social spending.

"Pakistan had taken important steps to strengthen its federal pension system, and this programme would help sustain and institutionalise those reforms,” said ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan.

stories.title: Three Sindh Public Service Commission officials dismissed for violating recruitment rules
summary: HYDERABAD: The Sindh Public Service Commission (SPSC) has taken disciplinary action against officials it says were found to have compromised the integrity of its recruitment process, in an accountability drive launched by SPSC Chairman Rizwan Ahmed.
To uphold these principles, he ordered a thorough review of the commission’s records and a verification of complaints received from the public and other stakeholders”.
Candidates were urged to rely only on official SPSC channels and to report any suspicious approach or misrepresentation to the commission.

stories.title: Another plan to transform Karachi's Burns Road into ‘pedestrian’ food street
summary: A couple of years ago, authorities closed both tracks of Burns Road to turn it into a food street.

He said that the proposed project, with an estimated cost of Rs250 million, will focus on the comprehensive improvement, beautification and modernisation of Burns Road, one of the city’s most renowned culinary destinations.
The project will also seek to preserve the distinctive identity and historical character of Burns Road while introducing modern urban design elements and improved pedestrian facilities.

stories.title: Punjab govt panned by opposition over sugar, smog and wheat issues
summary: LAHORE: On the first day of the 47th session of the Punjab Assembly, the opposition grilled the government over the sugar export price, soaring wheat rates and the handling of smog, while two amendment bills were tabled.

Responding to questions on the aquaculture and fisheries department, Parliamentary Secretary Mian Imran Javed drew a sharp rebuke from opposition MPA Hassan Malik, who said the department in Khushab district had been running the same ageing vehicle since 1985.

Presenting the environment department’s performance on smog control, Parliamentary Secretary for Environment Kanwal Liaquat Advocate said smog had no single cause, citing cross-border pollution, brick kilns and traffic emissions.

stories.title: New Zealand suffer Santner blow ahead of India Tests
summary: New Zealand all-rounder and limited-overs captain Mitchell Santner was on Tuesday ruled out of the two-Test series against India after breaking a bone in his hand.
New Zealand host India in Wellington on Thursday to begin a two-Test series which concludes in Christchurch from November 27.
The series will see the two nations meet in red-ball cricket for the first time since New Zealand’s historic 3-0 Test series win in India in 2024.

stories.title: Punjab to sue Salik over graft claims against Maryam

Minister refuses to retract his remarks, apologise to CM; also serves defamation notice on Azma Bokhari Both the chief minister and the information minister had challenged Salik to resign.
Reply to CM’s notice In the reply filed through his counsel, Salik rejected the chief minister’s legal notice, saying it had no legal or factual basis.

stories.title: US confirms probing Megaspeed over chip exports
summary: The Commerce Department began a probe into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations, the statement said.
The following month, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on a "no sell" list, while US federal agents conducted an "on-site, in-person" check at the Singapore-based firm and interviewed Alice Huang.

The scandal has exposed a rift within the administration of US President Donald Trump, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accusing the Commerce Department of ignoring reports that Megaspeed was shifting Nvidia technology to China.

stories.title: Police constable martyred in targeted attack in Bannu
summary: A police constable was martyred after unidentified armed men opened fire on him near the Afghan Refugees Camp in Bannu on Tuesday morning, Assistant Sub-Inspector Shah Barat Khan confirmed.

The southern districts of K-P, particularly Bannu and Lakki Marwat, have witnessed repeated attacks on police personnel in recent months, with officers frequently targeted by unidentified gunmen while travelling or performing routine duties.
On October 31, three policemen were martyred in separate attacks in Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur, while armed men also abducted a head constable in Bannu.
